exposure: sequential use of Foley catheter after misoprostol
Misoprostol followed by Foley catheter placement for induction
cervical dilation <1 cm at start of induction
concurrent use of misoprostol and cervical Foley catheter
cohort: 364 women with singleton pregnancies, intact membranes, and an unfavorable cervix undergoing term induction
finding: Sequential use of a cervical Foley catheter after misoprostol for labor induction in women with an unfavorable cervix was associated with longer labor, higher cesarean rate, and increased NICU admission compared to misoprostol alone.
mod_finding: Women who required a Foley catheter after misoprostol had a higher cesarean rate.
